_doctrine: Which text-role models are VALIDATED for tool use — a platform SAFETY decision, the same list for every host, never a per-host choice. An entry is earned ONLY by passing the admission bench (brain/mastercode/runtime/model_bench.py) under the CURRENT suite version; a pass under an older matrix is history and does not count. Nothing in a pod can add to this list: a local model_bench pass is information for the user, not a standing. This file lives in brain/ because brain/ is what the image ships; changing it is a PR, reviewed like any other change to what ships to everyone. Every OpenAI id is validated one by one; none is grandfathered.
_gate: When `enforce` is true (brain/mastercode/runtime/model_validation.py): a chat role on an unvalidated model keeps chat and its read tools and loses operate, dispatch and the host's build doors — and no dispatched agent starts either, because since the three-role cut (2026-09-19) an agent runs on the chat route rather than a seat of its own, so the chat model IS the agent's model. A dispatch that names its own model is gated on that model instead. chat is therefore the only role the gate can take anything from; review makes tool-less completions only. When false the gate observes only — catalog and routing status say who is validated, diagnostics raise a fault for an unvalidated route, nothing is withheld. It ships FALSE so landing the gate cannot strip a running host's tools before the platform has benched the models in use; flipping it is this one field, reviewed.
_entry_shape: {provider, model, suite_version, suite_hash, run_id, at, by} — provider as the Keys registry id or 'local'; model as the provider spells it WITHOUT a vendor prefix that repeats the provider (write anthropic + claude-opus-5, never anthropic + anthropic/claude-opus-5; the lookup drops such a prefix on both sides). A model is the weights it runs on: openrouter/X does NOT validate local/X — validate the local serving on its own. suite_version/suite_hash from the run record (model_bench_runs); run_id + at from that record; by = who ran it (the operator's host).
